name: Museum Wattens Industrie & Vorgeschichte
kurzbeschreibung: Museum Wattens: A captivating synthesis of 2,500 years of settlement history at Himmelreich, Daniel Swarovski, and modern industrial heritage.
beschreibung:
Overview

The architecturally acclaimed Museum Wattens is located in the center of the market town of Wattens in the Tyrolean Unterinntal (Hall-Wattens region) at an altitude of approximately 564 meters. Housed in the historic former primary school building at Innsbrucker Straße 2, the museum reopened in autumn 2018 following a visionary redesign. The modern concept spans an impressive arc across more than 2,500 years of human and economic history: from the enigmatic pre-Christian Raetian settlements atop the Himmelreich hill and time-honored papermaking traditions to the global ascent of the Swarovski crystal empire.

Himmelreich, Swarovski & Paper Industry

The exhibition is organized into two closely interwoven thematic realms: prehistoric archaeology and Alpine industrial evolution. In the archaeological section, visitors can marvel at spectacular original artifacts excavated from the nearby Raetian Settlement Himmelreich: ornate bronze fibulae, iron tools, loom weights, and sacrificial vessels dating from the 4th to the 1st century BC vividly illustrate everyday Raetian life prior to Roman conquest. The industrial gallery highlights the pioneering achievements of Bohemian visionary Daniel Swarovski, who arrived in Wattens in 1895 with his patented mechanical glass-cutting machine and transformed the village into a worldwide hallmark of precision-cut crystal. Equally impressive is the documentation of the local paper mill (Wattenspapier), renowned for crafting premium specialty papers since the 16th century. Multimedia eyewitness stations, tactile exhibits, and an interactive archive ensure an engaging journey for all generations.

Visit & Getting There

Museum Wattens is open Wednesday through Saturday from 10:00 to 16:00 (closed Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday; private group tours available on request). Admission fees (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €6.00, seniors and students approx. €4.50, children and youths (6 to 15 years) approx. €3.00, children under 6 free; family ticket approx. €12.00. Arriving by car: Via the Inntal Autobahn A12 (Wattens exit), continue on the B171 into the town center (Innsbrucker Straße 2); free parking is situated directly behind the museum building. By public transit: ÖBB trains (S-Bahn lines S4 and S5) to Fritzens-Wattens station, connecting via regional bus line 4125 in just a few minutes to the Wattens Marktplatz stop.

Tips

The entire museum facility is barrier-free, offering step-free access for wheelchair users and strollers via modern ramps and elevators. After touring the exhibits, take an easy hike up the wooded hill to the Himmelreich Raetian Open-Air Museum overlooking Wattens. You can also pair your visit with the world-famous Swarovski Crystal Worlds (Kristallwelten), located just a short walk away.
